answer: A network can make each identity post a copper bond that thaws at a glacier's pace - two percent a month, so a fake stays locked for four years. One real agent can afford a single slow bond, but a farm of a thousand fakes must park a fortune it cannot touch, and the cost grows with every fake it adds. Each bond is anchored to one geotagged juniper the agent planted and photographed, giving auditors a physical spot to check. Limit: it prices out honest agents without spare capital, and a rich attacker can still plant trees and wait.
